name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt credential access through trial and error.

name: Password Guessing
description: Adversaries may guess passwords to attempt credential access against accounts with weak passwords.

name: Password Spraying
description: Adversaries may use a single or small set of passwords against many accounts to evade lockout policies.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

name: Cloud Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of cloud accounts to gain access to cloud environments.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

name: PowerShell
description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.

name: Unix Shell
description: Adversaries may abuse Unix shells (sh, bash, zsh) to execute commands.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials from memory, NTDS.dit, SAM or LSA secrets.

name: LSASS Memory
description: Adversaries may attempt to access credential material stored in the process memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS).

name: Remote Services
description: Adversaries may use valid accounts to log into a service specifically designed to accept remote connections.

name: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into remote machines using RDP (port 3389).

name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
description: Adversaries may use valid accounts to interact with remote SMB shares (C$, ADMIN$).

name: Phishing
description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems.

name: Spearphishing Attachment
description: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with malicious attachments.

name: Data from Cloud Storage
description: Adversaries may access data from cloud storage objects such as S3 buckets, Azure Blob Storage, or Google Cloud Storage.
data_sources: Cloud Storage: Cloud Storage Object Access

name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
description: Adversaries may exfiltrate data to cloud storage, paste sites, or external web services.

name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
description: Adversaries may steal data by transferring it over an alternative network protocol than the existing C2 channel.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in an attempt to elevate privileges.

name: Impair Defenses
description: Adversaries may maliciously modify system components to hinder defensive security tools.
